newsitem.title: UK: Treasuries steady in London in low volumes.
newsitem.headline: Treasuries steady in London in low volumes.

text.p: U.S. Treasuries were quiet in London on Friday with prices little moved and only a small volume of transactions, traders said

"It is a typical Friday in the summer," a trader at a U.S. bank here said. "There has been predictable Asian central bank buying in the intermediate sector, but it hasn't been anywhere near as heavy as it was two days ago. The market is right down where it was at the close and...volumes are way below average."
At 0947 GMT the long bond was at 95-20 to yield 6.975 percent, compared with 95-20 in Tokyo and 95-19 at the New York close.
Two-year T-notes were at 99-30 to yield 6.284 percent, unchanged from Tokyo and up slightly from 99-29 in New York. Five-year T-notes were at 99-20, yielding 6.582 percent also unchanged from Tokyo.
Andrew Davies, bond analyst at London Bond Broking in London, said the five-year T-note auction on Thursday had gone slightly better than expected which had encouraged the market.
He said Treasuries had also benefited from some safe haven buying following the difficulties facing the move towards European monetary Union.
"There seems to have been a small amount of further buying in Tokyo which pushed the long-bond yield down to 6.98 percent," he said.
"There is a gently firm undertone in Treasuries and we are looking forward towards the data this afternoon," Davies said.
The first revision to U.S. first quarter GDP data were due at 1230 GMT, together with the price index and implicit deflator.
Davies said the effect of the better than expected trade numbers in March would tend to push the GDP numbers up.
Also due during the session were April new home sales figures at 1400 GMT, and the May Chicago Purchasing Managers Index.
A Reuters consensus of economists forecasts expected home sales to be 800,000 compared with 813,000 previously. The Chicago PMI was forecast to fall to 56.8 percent from 57.2 percent in April.
Davies said the medium term underlying tone of the market was a little bit cautious.
"Although the Fed didn't raise rates at the last FOMC, the market's mind set at the moment is that they expect them to put 25 basis points on it July," he said.
June T-bond futures were at 109-14, up 4/32 on the day in automated trade.
